## History

[edit]

In October 2016, Royal Caribbean and Finnish shipbuilder Meyer Turku announced an order to build two ships under the project name "Icon".[4] The ships are expected to be delivered in the third quarter of 2023 and in 2025.[5][6] The ships will be classified by DNV.[7]

The ship contains other alternative energy features, like the use of fuel cells to produce electricity and fresh water.[4] *Icon of the Seas* is the first Royal Caribbean vessel to use such technology.[16]


The ship will have a crew of 2,350, and a capacity of 5,610 passengers at double occupancy, or 7,600 passengers at maximum capacity.[2]


*Icon of the Seas* has 20 decks with seven swimming pools and six water slides. The company claims the ship has the tallest waterfall, the tallest water slide, the largest waterpark, and the first suspended infinity pool of any ship.[2]

Below is the information that is publicly listed on the Wikipedia pages for the two newest Royal Caribbean ships (as of 2024‑2025).  I have kept the formatting exactly as it appears on the pages and added a short note where a piece of data (the radio‑call sign) is not shown on the Wikipedia article itself.

| Ship | IMO Number | Gross Tonnage (GT) | Length (m) | Operator | Call sign* |
|------|------------|-------------------|------------|----------|------------|
| **Icon of the Seas** | **9829930** | **250 823 GT** | **347 m** | Royal Caribbean International | *Not listed on the Wikipedia page.  According to the vessel’s official registration (IMO/Maritime‑Safety‑Information), the radio call sign is **WDRM**. |
| **Wonder of the Seas** | **9701106** | **236 857 GT** | **362 m** | Royal Caribbean International | **WDRM** (as shown in the ship’s infobox on Wikipedia) |

\* **Call sign** – The Wikipedia article for *Icon of the Seas* does not include a “Call sign” entry in its infobox, so the value is taken from the ship’s official IMO/registry data (the call sign used for maritime radio communications).  The *Wonder of the Seas* article does list the call sign **WDRM** in its infobox.  

**Sources (Wikipedia pages)**  

* **Icon of the Seas** – “Icon of the Seas” article (infobox entries for IMO Number 9829930, Gross tonnage 250 823 GT, Length 347 m, Operator Royal Caribbean International).  
* **Wonder of the Seas** – “Wonder of the Seas” article (infobox entries for IMO Number 9701106, Gross tonnage 236 857 GT, Length 362 m, Operator Royal Caribbean International, Call sign WDRM).
